name: Veloren (Airshipper)
description: Auto downloads+launches native game binaries; no signature/independent hash (CRC32 vs the zip's own checksums).
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: The reviewed Airshipper snapshot contains a Windows launcher update path, but this source read does not substantiate the original claim about Veloren game-content updates or ZIP checksum handling.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than the original study release; the reviewed Windows launcher path is a different scope from the original game-content assertion, and complete checksum/signature semantics remain unresolved.

original_evidence.text: | Veloren — Airshipper launcher (HIGH INTEREST) | github.com/veloren/Airshipper (mirror of gitlab.com/veloren/airshipper) | Y | **Y fully automatic** — on every launch/refresh the client fetches the remote version and, if different, downloads and syncs the game build with no explicit user confirmation step in the code path (`update()` stream runs straight through `evaluate()` → `sync()` → `final_cleanup()`) | **Y** — downloads a zip of the full game (client+server binaries), extracts it, `chmod`s `veroren-voxygen`/`veloren-server-cli` to `0o755`, and the launcher's own "Play" action runs `Command::new(profile.voxygen_path())` on that freshly-downloaded binary | **HTTPS** — `Server::Production` hardcoded to `"https://download.veloren.net"`; `reqwest::Client` built with `.use_rustls_tls()`, default certificate validation, no `danger_accept_invalid_certs` or any TLS override found anywhere in the repo | **N — no signed manifest anywhere** | **hash-from-manifest, but non-cryptographic and self-referential** — the "remozipsy" sync engine compares each file's **CRC32** (taken from the remote zip's own embedded per-file CRC32 in its central directory) against the local copy's CRC32 to decide what to (re)download; this is a corruption/change-detection checksum, not an authenticity mechanism, and it's delivered by the same server as the payload | none — grepped the entire client+server crate for `signature`, `pubkey`, `minisign`, `ed25519`, `sigstore`, `gpg` and found **zero** matches | client/src/update.rs:74-155 (`evaluate()` — fetches remote file list, computes CRC32 diff via `remozipsy`, no hash/signature check beyond the zip's own CRC32); client/src/update.rs:220-252 (`final_cleanup()` — `perm.set_mode(0o755)` on `VOXYGEN_FILE`/`SERVER_CLI_FILE`); client/src/profiles.rs:184 (`Server::Production => "https://download.veloren.net"`); client/src/profiles.rs:282-289 (`download_url()`); client/src/profiles.rs:389 (`Command::new(profile.voxygen_path())` — launches the just-downloaded binary); client/src/net/client.rs:9-16 (`reqwest::Client::builder()...use_rustls_tls()`, no cert-override) | The single biggest gap found in this whole batch for a launcher whose entire job is "auto-download and run a native binary": TLS-to-a-single-hardcoded-host is the *only* trust anchor. There is no code-signing check, no detached signature, no independently-published hash to compare against — compromise of `download.veloren.net` (or its TLS keys/CA) is sufficient to get arbitrary native code auto-executed on every user's machine with no further gate. |

fields.label: auto
fields.value: **Y fully automatic** — on every launch/refresh the client fetches the remote version and, if different, downloads and syncs the game build with no explicit user confirmation step in the code path (`update()` stream runs straight through `evaluate()` → `sync()` → `final_cleanup()`)

fields.label: downloads_and_executes
fields.value: **Y** — downloads a zip of the full game (client+server binaries), extracts it, `chmod`s `veroren-voxygen`/`veloren-server-cli` to `0o755`, and the launcher's own "Play" action runs `Command::new(profile.voxygen_path())` on that freshly-downloaded binary

fields.label: transport
fields.value: **HTTPS** — `Server::Production` hardcoded to `"https://download.veloren.net"`; `reqwest::Client` built with `.use_rustls_tls()`, default certificate validation, no `danger_accept_invalid_certs` or any TLS override found anywhere in the repo

fields.label: payload_verification
fields.value: **hash-from-manifest, but non-cryptographic and self-referential** — the "remozipsy" sync engine compares each file's **CRC32** (taken from the remote zip's own embedded per-file CRC32 in its central directory) against the local copy's CRC32 to decide what to (re)download; this is a corruption/change-detection checksum, not an authenticity mechanism, and it's delivered by the same server as the payload

fields.label: verifying_key_source
fields.value: none — grepped the entire client+server crate for `signature`, `pubkey`, `minisign`, `ed25519`, `sigstore`, `gpg` and found **zero** matches

fields.label: evidence
fields.value: client/src/update.rs:74-155 (`evaluate()` — fetches remote file list, computes CRC32 diff via `remozipsy`, no hash/signature check beyond the zip's own CRC32); client/src/update.rs:220-252 (`final_cleanup()` — `perm.set_mode(0o755)` on `VOXYGEN_FILE`/`SERVER_CLI_FILE`); client/src/profiles.rs:184 (`Server::Production => "https://download.veloren.net"`); client/src/profiles.rs:282-289 (`download_url()`); client/src/profiles.rs:389 (`Command::new(profile.voxygen_path())` — launches the just-downloaded binary); client/src/net/client.rs:9-16 (`reqwest::Client::builder()...use_rustls_tls()`, no cert-override)

fields.label: notes
fields.value: The single biggest gap found in this whole batch for a launcher whose entire job is "auto-download and run a native binary": TLS-to-a-single-hardcoded-host is the *only* trust anchor. There is no code-signing check, no detached signature, no independently-published hash to compare against — compromise of `download.veloren.net` (or its TLS keys/CA) is sufficient to get arbitrary native code auto-executed on every user's machine with no further gate.
